subject.title: Bug: Poe image/video-output models are accepted in config but fail at runtime (Nano Banana 400, Veo/Sora fallback)

question: Should configured chat models that produce images or videos be rejected with a clear unsupported-output diagnostic, or should OpenClaw add first-class media-output chat model routing?
rationale: The current code supports input metadata and separate generation tools, but choosing where output modality belongs affects public config, provider catalogs, fallback behavior, docs, and channel delivery.

options.title: Reject media-output chat models now
options.body: Add an upgrade-safe guard and docs that treat image/video-output models as unsupported in chat/session runtime while pointing users to `image_generate` and `video_generate`.

options.title: Add first-class output routing
options.body: Introduce output-modality metadata and route media-producing models through generation response handling and channel delivery.

options.title: Document current split only
options.body: Clarify the existing separate-tool model without changing runtime behavior, leaving confusing fallback and malformed request cases possible.

recommendation.title: Reject media-output chat models now
recommendation.body: Add an upgrade-safe guard and docs that treat image/video-output models as unsupported in chat/session runtime while pointing users to `image_generate` and `video_generate`.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across media model metadata, provider identity, media-tool behavior, and docs that would constrain this decision.
